title.narrative: Enabling gender responsive blue and circular economy for coastal communities and the county aggregation and industrial parks in Nyamira and Laikipia Counties

description.narrative: Current agri-food systems are a major contributor to climate change and have in some instances had negative effects on the planetĀ“s biodiversity. According to a WRI report, wasted food takes a major financial toll, costing the global economy more than $ 1 trillion every year. It also fuels climate change, accounting for approximately 8%-10% of global greenhouse emissions. Food loss in Kenya can be extrapolated to amount to Ksh 72 billion lost annually for select crop value chains based on a study done by (FAO, 2018) and Ksh. 432 billion annually by not addressing food loss and waste and food losses in Sub-Saharan Africa. The common occurrence in Kenya is oversupply of produce, creating a challenge in marketing and resulting in huge losses The project aims to contribute to food security through maximizing resource recovery for enhanced economic, social and environmental gains by developing waste generation streams from the agri-food systems. This will be tested through developing sustainable resource utilization models and management of post-harvest losses by embedding circular economy principles in production and processing of banana <(>&<)> green leafy vegetables and meat value chains in the County Aggregation and Industrial Parks of Nyamira and Laikipia.
